notes: All eight packet elements are on the consumes side, so declares and not_declared are empty by rule. The seven api:rmw_* elements (rmw_create_guard_condition, rmw_create_subscription, rmw_create_wait_set, rmw_destroy_subscription, rmw_take_with_info, rmw_trigger_guard_condition, rmw_wait) are not named anywhere in the snapshot: an exact grep -rn over all files of snapshot/ (rclcpp, rclcpp_action, rclcpp_components, rclcpp_lifecycle, including tests and CMake) returned zero hits for each symbol. rclcpp reaches the corresponding functionality only through rcl: rcl_guard_condition_init (src/rclcpp/guard_condition.cpp:33), rcl_trigger_guard_condition (src/rclcpp/guard_condition.cpp:82), rcl_wait_set_init (src/rclcpp/executor.cpp:71, src/rclcpp/graph_listener.cpp:56, include/rclcpp/wait_set_policies/detail/storage_policy_common.hpp:95), rcl_wait (src/rclcpp/executor.cpp:750), rcl_subscription_init (src/rclcpp/subscription_base.cpp:67), rcl_subscription_fini (src/rclcpp/subscription_base.cpp:53), rcl_take (src/rclcpp/subscription_base.cpp:152). Because the code does not call the rmw_* symbols, they get no port and are in neither references nor declares; they are consumed only transitively via the rcl dependency. resource:node_notify_guard_condition is not one of the listed canonical-name kinds, but the packet names it and the code references it via NodeBaseInterface::get_notify_guard_condition(), so it is recorded in references and given a port. Its msg_type and definition_id are null because a guard condition has no message definition; QoS is null because the GuardCondition API has no QoS parameters (only rcl_guard_condition_options_t, include/rclcpp/guard_condition.hpp:50-54). The executor adds node notify guard conditions to its wait set through rclcpp::detail::add_guard_condition_to_rcl_wait_set (include/rclcpp/strategies/allocator_memory_strategy.hpp:235-236), which does not check in_use_by_wait_set_; GuardCondition::add_to_wait_set (the exclusive path) has no non-test caller in the snapshot, while rclcpp::WaitSet uses exchange_in_use_by_wait_set_state for guard conditions (include/rclcpp/wait_set_template.hpp:284). The exclusive tokens are software single-owner claims (node-to-executor, guard-condition-to-wait-set), not hardware or device handles.
